description: We are building an interactive space exploration game designed to make scientific discovery engaging through a progressive, level-based journey across 5+ levels. As a player progresses, real NASA facts pop up throughout the gameplay. By navigating environments, players earn points —allowing them to enhance their gear, ships, and tools, which is mandatory to survive harsher conditions and unlock challenging levels.
summary:
Mission Mars is a 2D educational game, built in Unity, that shows players what it takes to get humans to Mars and keep them alive there. It was made for the NASA Space Apps Challenge “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer”

Players work through five levels. They fly a spacecraft through an asteroid field, guide a rover through a maze, drive across the Martian surface avoiding rocks, connect pipes to keep the water level steady, and finally keep a colony running by tending its solar, shield and oxygen stations. Five 3D animated cutscenes made in Blender link the levels into one story, and each shares real facts about Mars, such as its low gravity, its cold, and dust storms that can block most of the sunlight.

The game turns a technical subject into something children can play, helping them understand the challenges of reaching Mars and living there.
details:
What it does and how it works

Mission Mars: Land & Explore is a 2D educational game, built in Unity, that takes players on a journey from Earth to a Martian colony. It has five levels: flying a spacecraft through an asteroid belt, guiding a rover through a maze, driving across the surface while avoiding rocks, connecting pipes to keep the water level steady, and keeping a colony running by tending its solar, shield and oxygen stations. Four 3D animated cutscenes made in Blender connect the levels into one story. Each level has its own goals and challenges, such as managing health, fuel, battery, time and resource levels.

Benefits and intended impact

The game turns a technical subject into something people can play. Players come away understanding what it takes to reach Mars and live there: the distance, the cold, the power and oxygen needed to survive. We hope it gets students and the public curious about human space exploration.

Tools and technology

Unity and C# for the game, Blender for the 3D transitions, and GitHub for teamwork. Unity Asset Store.

Use of NASA information

The Mars facts in the game come from NASA’s article “Humans to Mars,” including the round-trip distance, Mars’ gravity and temperature range, dust storms and solar power. Each level is tied to one of these facts.

Creativity

Instead of presenting facts as a lesson, we built each one into a mechanic. Dust storms threaten the colony’s power, oxygen is something the player has to keep up, and water has to be routed with pipes. The cinematic transitions add a story that the 2D levels alone couldn’t tell.

Factors we considered

Accuracy of the facts.

Keeping the levels varied and easy to learn.

The time available.
